title: Multiplexer Module - WiFi 5 GHz for Automotive V2X Communication
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Sarah Okonkwo

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Multiplexer Module filter targeting WiFi 5 GHz for Automotive V2X Communication. The filter is designed on 42° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 5991.9 MHz and bandwidth of 396.9 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Automotive V2X Communication module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Multiplexer Module
- Frequency Band: WiFi 5 GHz
- Application: Automotive V2X Communication
- Substrate: 42° YX LiTaO3
- Package: SiP (System in Package)
- Design Tool: Synopsys CustomSim
- Design Center: Helsinki 5G Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Multiplexer Module design targeting WiFi 5 GHz. Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       5991.9 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       396.9 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 19.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 47.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 44.0 dB
Q Factor:               8394
Temperature Coefficient:-9.8 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.5 x 1.6 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   5
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Synopsys CustomSim and load the Multiplexer Module template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 42° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 5991.9 MHz, BW 396.9 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (SiP (System in Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 42° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 17976 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 19.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 595 MHz offset >= 47.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 2 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 7.3 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +28 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 95%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-08-23
Devices Tested:         32
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.19 dB
Return Loss (meas):     20.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       50.3 dB
Isolation (meas):       49.3 dB
Q Factor (meas):        8394
Group Delay Variation:  3.2 ns
Power Handling:         +30 dBm
Die Yield:              92.7%

Result Classification:  PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Multiplexer Module design demonstrated excellent performance for WiFi 5 GHz.
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Group delay flatness improved compared to previous revision.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Design passed all acceptance criteria.
